chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Low-LET gamma (Cs-137 662 keV; Co-60); most biologically significant DNA lesion; DSB = both strands of DNA double helix broken within ~10-20 base pairs; in Chernobyl context: at 1 Gy (0.7 Gy ARS threshold) a cell has ~40 DSBs; at 200 mSv (average liquidator) ~8 DSBs per cell
notes: Misrepaired DSBs = chromosomal aberrations, translocations, point mutations; inaccurate NHEJ creates deletions; DSBs are the primary molecular mechanism linking radiation dose to cancer risk; each Chernobyl liquidator at 117 mSv: ~4-5 DSBs per somatic cell at exposure
source: Lobrich M 2010 Nat Rev Cancer PMID:20393565; ICRU 60; Ward JF 1988 Progr Nucleic Acid Res

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Much more common than DSBs but easily repaired using complementary strand as template; ~25x more SSBs than DSBs; SSBs repaired by BER (base excision repair) in minutes to hours; rarely cause permanent damage
notes: For Chernobyl context: at 1 Gy: 1000 SSBs, 40 DSBs, ~2000 base damages per cell; SSBs repaired so quickly they are generally not the limiting factor in radiation carcinogenesis
source: Ward 1988; Cadet J 2003 Mutation Res PMID:12649923; BEIR V 1990

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Oxidized purines (8-oxo-guanine) and pyrimidines; ring-opened bases; formamidopyrimidines; repaired by base excision repair (BER); if unrepaired: G→T transversions (most common); 8-oxo-G lesions specifically produced by OH• radical from water radiolysis
notes: Radiation-induced base damage is primarily from hydroxyl radical (OH•): H2O + radiation → H2O+ + e-aq → OH• in water radiolysis; ~80% of DNA damage via OH•; 20% direct energy deposition on DNA; explains why hydration state affects radiosensitivity
source: Cadet 2003; Ward 1988; Milligan 1993 Free Radic Res

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: At 1 Gy in water: ~0.28 µmol/L OH•; ~0.28 µmol/L eaq; ~0.07 µmol/L H2O2; ~0.06 µmol/L H•; sparsely ionizing gamma radiation (Cs-137 Co-60) produces mostly SSBs and base damage; densely ionizing alpha (Pu Am actinides) produces clusters of damage (DSB clusters) along particle track → harder to repair
notes: This explains why alpha emitters (Pu-239 in hot particles at Chernobyl) are 20x more carcinogenic per Gy than gamma radiation; clustered DSBs overwhelm NHEJ repair; RBE(alpha)=20 for induction of lung cancer (ICRP 122 2013)
source: von Sonntag 2006 Free-Radical-Induced DNA Damage; ICRU 60; ICRP 122 2013

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Dominant DSB repair pathway in G1 (post-mitotic or G1 cells = most somatic cells at any time); fast but error-prone; KU70/KU80 heterodimer binds DSB ends; DNA-PKcs activates; XRCC4/LIG4 ligation; misjoining = translocation = oncogenic potential; also called 'fast component' of repair kinetics
notes: NHEJ operates throughout cell cycle but especially G1; Cancer risk from radiation = NHEJ misrepair → translocations → proto-oncogene activation or tumor suppressor inactivation; specific example: t(2;5) in ALCL from misrepaired DSBs; Chernobyl papillary thyroid cancers show specific inv(10)(q11.2q21) rearrangement (RET/PTC)
source: Lieber MR 2010 Annu Rev Biochem PMID:20192759; Bhatt 2012 Nature Immunol

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: High-fidelity DSB repair using sister chromatid as template; only operates in S and G2 phases (after DNA replication when sister exists); RAD51-dependent strand invasion; ~5x more accurate than NHEJ; important for radiation-induced cancer: BRCA1/BRCA2 deficiency → impaired HR → elevated breast/ovarian cancer risk
notes: HR relevance to Chernobyl: liquidators and contaminated population with BRCA1/2 variants hypothetically at higher radiation-induced cancer risk; no specific studies of this interaction in Chernobyl cohorts identified; general principle of radiation × genetic susceptibility
source: Symington LS 2011 Nat Rev Mol Cell Biol PMID:22009060; Bhatt 2012

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Chernobyl-specific thyroid cancer molecular signature: inv(10)(q11.2q21) creates RET/PTC1 or RET/PTC3 gene rearrangement; RET proto-oncogene fuses with CCDC6 (PTC1) or ELE1 (PTC3); papillary thyroid carcinoma in Chernobyl children shows RET/PTC at higher frequency than sporadic adult PTC; this is the molecular link between I-131 beta particle dose to thyroid and cancer initiation
notes: RET/PTC rearrangements specifically arise from radiation-induced DSBs bringing RET and CCDC6 or ELE1 into proximity; beta particle from I-131 deposits dose in small thyroid follicular cell = clustered DSBs in small nucleus → higher probability of misrepair joining distant loci
source: Nikiforov YE 2003 Endocrine-Related Cancer PMID:14598823; Elisei R 2001; thyroid_cancer_timeseries_REAL.csv

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Non-irradiated cells adjacent to irradiated cells show DNA damage (micronuclei, γH2AX foci); mediated by: gap junctions (direct cell-cell communication); secreted signaling molecules (ROS, NO, TGF-β, cytokines); operative in vitro and in vivo in some tissues; potential to increase effective biological range beyond directly irradiated cells
notes: Controversy: bystander effect well-established in vitro; population-level significance at Chernobyl doses uncertain; some models suggest bystander effect explains why LNT underestimates effects at very low doses; others argue it contributes to adaptive response (hormesis); not included in ICRP risk models currently
source: Mothersill C 2001 Radiat Res PMID:11389803; Prise KM 2009 Nat Rev Cancer PMID:19629072

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Cells descended from irradiated cells show elevated mutation rates many cell divisions later; persists in offspring cells; mediated by: epigenetic changes; oxidative stress; altered DNA methylation; potentially contributes to radiation carcinogenesis at low doses; documented in vitro; animal studies; some liquidator cytogenetic data
notes: If genomic instability is real in vivo at Chernobyl doses: it would explain why cancer risk might be higher than pure DSB model predicts; contested mechanism; UNSCEAR 2012 LOW DOSE report considers it biologically plausible but uncertain at low doses
source: Morgan WF 2003 Radiat Res PMID:12880536; Kadhim 1992 Nature; UNSCEAR 2012 ANNEX C

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Low-LET radiation (Cs-137 662 keV gamma; I-131 beta): ~0.3 keV/µm; sparsely ionizing; primarily SSBs and base damage; High-LET (Pu-239 alpha 5.15 MeV; Am-241 alpha 5.49 MeV; fission neutrons): 80-100 keV/µm; dense ionization track; DSB clusters; high RBE
notes: RBE (Relative Biological Effectiveness): gamma reference = 1; alpha = 20 (ICRP weighting factor wR); neutron = 5-20 (energy dependent); This is why Pu-239 and Am-241 alpha emitters are so concerning as hot particles: same absorbed dose → 20x more DNA damage; hot particle inhalation dose underestimated by dose (Gy) units alone
source: ICRP 103 2007 Table 2 weighting factors; ICRU 36 1983; fuel_particle_contamination_REAL.csv; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Radiosensitivity varies: G2/M most sensitive (chromosomes condensed; no sister chromatid for HR; damage most likely to result in mitotic catastrophe); G1 next; S phase relatively resistant; G0 very resistant; thyroid follicular cells actively cycling in children → higher radiosensitivity; explains age-specific I-131 thyroid cancer risk
notes: Children have higher cell proliferation rates → more cells in G2/M → higher probability that radiation DSBs produce catastrophic chromosomal aberrations; adult thyroid cells mostly G0 → lower cancer risk per unit dose; this is independent reason why children more sensitive than adults to I-131
source: Hall EJ Giaccia AJ Radiobiology for the Radiologist 2018; dose_conversion_factors_REAL.csv; unscear_evacuee_thyroid_doses_REAL.csv

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Low doses (20-200 mGy) may induce DNA repair enzymes and antioxidant defenses that reduce subsequent radiation sensitivity; documented in vitro; some animal studies; disputed for in vivo human populations; used by hormesis advocates to argue Chernobyl doses cause no harm or even benefit; counterargument: adaptive response at cellular level does not necessarily prevent cancer at organism level
notes: No definitive human epidemiology evidence for adaptive response preventing Chernobyl-related cancer below 200 mGy; ICRP maintains LNT despite adaptive response mechanisms; UNSCEAR 2012 LOW DOSE: 'it is not possible to say whether adaptive responses are important determinants of health effects in human populations exposed to low doses'
source: Parsons WD 2008 Adv Anat Embryol Cell Biol; Mitchel REJ 2003 Dose-Response PMID:24818920; UNSCEAR 2012 LOW DOSE Annex B

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: γH2AX (phosphorylated histone H2AX at Ser139) forms at each DSB within minutes; serves as sensitive biomarker for DSBs and DNA damage; foci count can detect doses as low as 1-10 mGy in irradiated cells; useful for retrospective biodosimetry; applied to Chernobyl cleanup workers and contaminated population
notes: γH2AX biodosimetry: can detect radiation exposure weeks to months after irradiation (persistent foci); applied in some Chernobyl follow-up studies; see retrospective_dosimetry_methods_REAL.csv for methods; γH2AX + FISH cytogenetics = most sensitive methods for low-dose retrospective dosimetry in humans

chernobyl_or_radiation_relevance: Radiation-induced telomere shortening and instability documented in Chernobyl liquidators; possibly via oxidative stress and radiation-induced oxidative damage to telomeric DNA (G-rich sequences highly susceptible to 8-oxo-G formation); longer-term biomarker of radiation exposure
notes: Telomere length in peripheral blood leukocytes: shorter in high-dose liquidators vs controls in some studies; may contribute to increased cancer risk; also associated with cardiovascular disease (consistent with CVD excess in liquidators); telomere shortening is independent of LNT and provides mechanistic support for radiation-CVD link
source: Hande MP 2003 Radiat Res PMID:12697838; Serak VA 2019; liquidator_noncancer_effects_REAL.csv
